fixes.explanation: Kadesh-barnea is where they arrive. The text says that after the vast and terrifying wilderness, they reached it. It's also where Moses speaks to them about the hill country. Hang on to that name, baker, because it comes back at the end of the passage.

Right, he never tells them to wait for a sign. What he says is, “See, the LORD your God has placed the land before you.” Then comes the order to go up and take possession of it, as the LORD has told them. That's a go-up kind of speech, and I'd be bouncing on my base, ready to roll.

Greedy isn't the word Moses uses. He says, “Do not be afraid or discouraged.” I think fear is what he has on his mind here, not wanting too much. Keep that in mind, because fear keeps coming back in this story.

The people ask for men who will “…bring us word of what route to follow and which cities to enter.” They want directions, plain and simple. It sounds like a very reasonable ask to me. I'd want a map too, and I'd want it laminated.

No treaty comes up in this request. The people ask for men to search out the land and bring word of what route to follow and which cities to enter. That's a scouting request, not a treaty request. They want information.

Gifts aren't part of what the people ask for. They want the men to search out the land and bring word of the route and the cities. The request is about information, not presents. Keep reading, because the spies do bring something back.
Moses says, “…I selected twelve men from among you, one from each tribe.” That's one man for every tribe. He also says the plan seemed good to him.

Seventy isn't the number. Moses says he selected twelve men from among them, one from each tribe. That's one man for each tribe, twelve in all. Check that verse again, friend, and the number will stick.

Weapons aren't what the text names. It says they took some of the fruit of the land in their hands and carried it down. Fruit is what the verse puts in their hands. That's what came down to the people.

Not straight up. After the report, Moses says, “…you were unwilling to go up; you rebelled against the command of the LORD your God.” Then he says they grumbled in their tents. They do go up into the hill country later in the passage, but that comes after the LORD speaks.

Correct, they don't head up at that point. Moses says they were unwilling to go up, and he calls it rebelling against the command of the LORD. The spies had said it was a good land, and the people grumbled in their tents anyway. Keep your ears open, baker, because there's more to hear.

Those are the people's own words. They say the LORD brought them out of Egypt “…to deliver us into the hand of the Amorites to be annihilated.” They say it in their tents, and they begin with, “Because the LORD hates us…” Moses is retelling what they said.

True. In their grumbling, the people repeat what their brothers said: “The people are larger and taller than we are…” They add that the cities are large, with walls up to the heavens. The people say their brothers made their hearts melt.

Moses says the LORD carried them “…as a man carries his son, all the way by which you traveled until you reached this place.” That's a picture of a father and his boy. I like that picture a lot. And Moses says it covers all the way they traveled.

A load isn't the picture. Moses says the LORD carried them in the wilderness “…as a man carries his son…” It's a father and a son, not a servant and a load. And Moses says it covers all the way they traveled until they reached this place.
Moses says the LORD went before them “…in the fire by night and in the cloud by day…” So it was fire for the night and cloud for the day. And Moses says it was to show them the road to travel.

It's true. Moses says the LORD went before them “…to seek out a place for you to camp and to show you the road to travel.” He wasn't only pointing the direction. He was also seeking out places for them to camp.

The LORD says Caleb son of Jephunneh will see the land “…because he followed the LORD wholeheartedly.” Wholeheartedly means all in. That's the reason the LORD gives for Caleb. He adds that He will give Caleb and his descendants the land on which he has set foot.

The LORD says, “Encourage him, for he will enable Israel to inherit the land.” That's the instruction to Moses about Joshua son of Nun. The reason given is that Joshua will enable Israel to inherit the land.

Warn isn't what the LORD says. The word is “Encourage him, for he will enable Israel to inherit the land.” The LORD says Joshua will enter the land and will enable Israel to inherit it. Moses' instruction is to encourage him.

The LORD says, “But you are to turn back and head for the wilderness along the route to the Red Sea.” So the direction is back toward the wilderness. I think that's a hard order to hear. A turn-around is a turn-around.

Egypt isn't named in this order. The LORD tells them to turn back and head for the wilderness along the route to the Red Sea. Egypt is where the LORD brought them out of, but this order points to the wilderness.

True. Moses says each man put on his weapons of war, “…thinking it easy to go up into the hill country.” Earlier the people said the cities had walls up to the heavens. Now they think going up is easy, and I think that's quite a swing.

It's true. The text says each man put on his weapons of war, “…thinking it easy to go up into the hill country.” Compare that with the people earlier saying the cities were large, with walls up to the heavens. Now the thought is that it's easy. That's quite a swing, and I can't help noticing it.
The LORD says, “…I am not with you to keep you from defeat by your enemies.” That's the reason He gives for this fight: He is not with them. So He tells them not to go up and fight.

Moses says he spoke to them, and they would not listen. Then he says they rebelled against the command of the LORD and presumptuously went up into the hill country. They refused the warning, baker, and then they climbed.
No second sign is mentioned. Moses says he spoke to them, and they would not listen. Then they rebelled against the command of the LORD and went up into the hill country.

Nothing like that is in the passage. Moses says he spoke to them, they would not listen, and they went up into the hill country. Whether Moses went along isn't something these verses say. What they say is that the people rebelled against the command of the LORD.

Peace isn't what Moses reports. The Amorites who lived in the hills came out against Israel, and the chase ran from Seir to Hormah. Moses says it was “…like a swarm of bees.” I think this part is heavy.
